NEPHROLOGY NOTE   Date: 2026-10-21
57M, ambulatory visit for a scheduled nephrology problem evaluation.

S:
Patient presents for routine nephrology follow-up. He reports that his energy has been low over the past several weeks, with swelling in both ankles that worsens by evening and improves overnight. He has been following the low-sodium plan and checking his weight at home. Appetite is reduced but adequate. He takes all medications as prescribed and has had no trouble obtaining refills. He reports being unable to keep a regular work schedule and missed 5 days of work last month. Denies chest pain. He works as a bus mechanic and says standing for long stretches has become harder. Lives with his wife, who helps track his daily weights. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 134/82, HR 74, RR 16, Temp 98.0 F, SpO2 97% on room air. Weight 192 lb, up 3 lb from prior.
General: tired appearing, in no acute distress.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no rub.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: trace to 1+ bilateral ankle edema.
Labs (this week): creatinine 2.7 mg/dL, eGFR 22 mL/min/1.73m2, potassium 4.9 mmol/L, bicarbonate 21 mmol/L, phosphorus 4.5 mg/dL. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 380 mg/g.

A/P:
1. Chronic kidney disease stage 4, eGFR 22, followed by nephrology. Labs reviewed with patient. Continue ACE inhibitor with close potassium monitoring. Reinforced low-sodium, moderate-protein diet; dietitian referral updated. Discussed long-term planning and education on future treatment options; written materials provided.
2. Daily weights: weight is up 3 lb from the last visit. Advised daily weights and to call for a gain over 3 lb in two days. Diuretic dose reviewed and continued.
3. Function and work: reduced activity tolerance is affecting his usual schedule. Provided a letter describing current limits for his employer.

Repeat labs in 6 weeks. Return to clinic in 3 months, sooner for worsening swelling or reduced urine output.
